newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran appoints new commander of ground forces.
newsitem.headline: Iran appoints new commander of ground forces.

text.p: Iran has appointed a new acting chief of the army's ground forces, Iranian newspapers said on Tuesday.
The daily Salam said Brigadier-General Abdolali Pourshasb was named acting chief of the army's ground forces, replacing commander Brigadier-General Ahmad Dadbin.
Dadbin and his deputy, Brigadier-General Karim Ebadat, were appointed advisers to Army Chief-of-Staff Major-General Ali Shahbazi, the newspaper said.
Dadbin had held the post since his appointment in October 1994 by Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, who is also commander-in-chief of the country's armed forces.

The Iranian regular army's ground forces consist of about 350,000 men, including some 250,000 conscripts, according to Western military experts. The country's Revolutionary Guards, set up after the 1979 Islamic revolution, have an estimated 120,000 men.
